title: Orlando Whole-Home Remodel: Kitchen, Baths and Floors
highlights:
# Inside an Orlando Whole-Home Remodel: Kitchen, Two Bathrooms, Entertainment Wall and Floors
...
When a remodel covers a kitchen, two bathrooms, an entertainment wall and every floor in the house, the hard part is not any single room. It is making sure they all still belong to the same house when the last piece of trim goes on.
...
This Orlando home came to us wearing the palette it was built with: dark cherry cabinetry, granite counters, and beige ceramic tile running room to room. None of it was failing. It was simply a long way behind how the family actually used the house. We took the kitchen, the primary bathroom, the pool bathroom, the family room’s entertainment wall and the flooring throughout as one scope — which is the only way a whole-house palette holds together. The walkthrough above runs just under a minute.
...
From the family room, the old kitchen was something you looked past, not into. A raised granite breakfast bar
...
working side, four stools pulled up outside it, a tall pier of cut-out
...
beside them.
...
it sat dark cherry
...
of a tall ceiling, a pair
...
bi-fold
...
The bar and the pier both came out, and the kitchen is completely open to the family room now. The new island replaces that arrangement at one level: a single long rectangle seating five along one side, the sink set into it, so whoever is working there faces the room instead of standing behind a bar. The perimeter cabinetry is a soft cream, taken all the way up this time, with glass-front uppers lit from inside and the ovens built flush into the run. The hood is finished as cabinetry rather than dropped in as an appliance. Counters and the backsplash behind the cooktop are the same pale slab with soft grey veining; the hardware, faucets and all three pendants over the island are brass.
...
The sink is a workstation run with an integrated ledge, so the cutting board, colander and drying rack sit down into it rather than on the counter — which earns its keep in a kitchen where the island is where people gather.
...
The detail most people notice last is the laundry: behind dark-stained slatted wood doors beside the refrigerator, reading as millwork rather than a utility door.
...
The primary bathroom had the most floor area to work with and the least to show for it. A corner drop-in tub sat on the diagonal in a tiled deck in the middle of the room, with a separate shower stall beyond it. A dark cherry double vanity ran the opposite wall under granite and a tall glass block window; the floor was the same beige tile as everywhere else.
...
The tub is gone, and so is the glass block. The shower took that end of the room instead: a wide walk-in behind a single glass panel, with a ceiling-mounted rain head, a handheld on a slide bar, and a full wall of white tile in a raised, organic pattern that catches the light differently as the day moves. It is the only pattern in the room, which is why it can be that large.
...
The vanity is now a floating run in a medium wood: two undermount sinks under a pale slab, brass fittings, one mirror across the whole length instead of two. The floor is a large-format tile with soft grey veining. Nothing in the room sits on a diagonal any more.
...
The pool bathroom gets used wet, which changes what the finishes have to do. The old version had a dark vanity under a dark solid counter, a black-framed mirror, and a tub-shower behind a curtain with a half wall between it and the toilet.
...
The layout stayed. Almost everything else did not. Stacked tile in a warm greige now runs to the ceiling around the tub and wraps the half wall, with a recessed niche and a brass frame finishing the glass panel above. The rain head comes off a swan-necked brass arm, and a curtain still runs on a brass rod — off a pool deck, a curtain serves better than a door.
...
The vanity is from the same wood family as the primary bath, with a full-height linen tower beside it — the storage this room never had — and two floating shelves opposite. The counter is a pale slab; the floor is a large-format light tile that can take wet feet.
...
The family room had a television on a grey painted accent wall, a soundbar beneath it, and nothing else. It was the largest surface in the room and it was doing no work.
...
Now dark-stained slatted wood runs floor to ceiling in two panels flanking a plain centre section, so the television sits in the quiet part of the wall and the texture happens around it. A solid wood shelf crosses the full width, deep enough to be useful, thin enough not to read as furniture. Two vertical sconces with stone shades and exposed tube bulbs wash light down the slats after dark, when the wall does its best work.
...
It is the same dark slatted wood as the laundry doors in the kitchen — not a coincidence, but the thread
...
the two ends of the house together.
...
Every room above sits on a new floor, and that is what made the four read as one house, not four projects.
...
The beige ceramic tile came out everywhere. Wide-plank wood in a warm, light tone now runs through the kitchen, the dining area and the family room with no threshold anywhere in the sightline. The bathrooms went to large-format tile, as wet rooms should — the primary in a soft grey veined stone look, the pool bath in a light neutral — and still read as continuous because the tone carries.
...
Flooring is the least photogenic line on a remodel proposal and the one you feel most, walking from one end of a house to the other.
...
If you are planning a kitchen remodel, a bathroom remodel, or a whole-house project in Orlando, Winter Park, Windermere or anywhere in Central Florida, we would like to hear what you are hoping to change. Design and construction are handled by one team here, so the plan you approve is the plan that gets built.

title: He Spray-Painted the Oak Cabinets Neptune Lily and Made the Original Kitchen Look New
highlights:
He Spray-Painted the Oak Cabinets Neptune Lily and Made the Original Kitchen Look New
...
He Spray-Painted the Oak Cabinets Neptune Lily and Made the Original Kitchen Look New

 

Warm oak covered almost every cabinet in this kitchen, from the long run beneath the windows to the tall appliance units and island. Instead of removing cabinetry that already fit the room, the existing doors, drawer fronts, frames, end panels, wine storage, and decorative details were kept for a color change.
...
Instagram creator @renewingdecorating spray-painted the cabinetry in Neptune Lily, replacing the orange-toned oak finish with a pale neutral shade. Granite countertops, exposed brick, dark ceiling beams, wood flooring, and the kitchen layout remained, making the cabinet color the change that separates the before and after.
...
The finished kitchen still has the same raised-panel doors, tall storage, glass-front wall cabinet, island shelving, and built-in appliances seen in the original room. Against the new cabinet finish, the brick and old timber beams become stronger features instead of competing with another warm wood tone.
...
Before the repaint, oak ran across the base cabinets, wall cabinet, tall units, and island, giving several parts of the kitchen the same warm brown tone. The island brought even more wood into the center of the room, with vertical paneling on its sides and open storage facing the living area.
...
Its front was built around two narrow sets of cubbies with a larger opening in the middle. Those details become useful
...
points in the after photos because the same arrangement remains after the color change.
...
Another cabinet run sits against an exposed red brick wall, with a gas cooktop set into the dark granite counter. Oak doors and drawers filled the area below while the brick itself served as the backsplash.
...
Painting this section would create a much sharper break between the cabinetry and masonry. Rather than having brown wood meet red and brown brick, the new finish separates the two materials while leaving the original wall exposed.
...
Cabinetry beside the sink extended from floor to ceiling around the built-in ovens, creating one of the largest blocks of oak in the room. Matching base cabinets continued beneath the window and around the corner toward the utility area.
...
Dark granite counters, stainless hardware, appliances, and the sink were already in place, so changing the cabinetry did not require a new layout to alter the room’s appearance.
...
Viewed from the opposite side, the island shows how much of its original construction survived the makeover. Wine cubbies flank the center opening, narrow dividers break up the shelves, and a shaped wood detail sits beneath the countertop.
...
Rather than replacing those features, the repaint treats them as part of the new design. Their shapes remain visible after the oak grain disappears beneath the Neptune Lily finish.
...
Cabinet doors were removed and taken into a spray booth, where they were suspended before receiving the Neptune Lily finish. Spraying the doors away from the cabinet boxes allowed the paint to cover the recessed panels, narrow edges, and outer frames without the hardware or surrounding kitchen getting in the way.
...
The smooth finish seen here also explains why the completed cabinets can look like new units at first glance. Once the doors returned to the kitchen, the oak grain disappeared beneath an even coat while the original door profiles remained.
...
After spray painting, the same island, wall cabinet, base units, and tall oven cabinetry appear in Neptune Lily. Raised-panel doors and the island’s open storage remain easy to identify, but the pale finish removes the continuous oak tone that once ran through the room.
...
Dark granite was left in place, creating a narrow contrasting line across the pale cabinets. Existing wood flooring also remains, so natural wood is still present without covering the vertical surfaces around the kitchen.
...
The change is clear at the cooktop, where Neptune Lily now sits beneath the original granite counter and exposed brick. Drawer sizes, door profiles, plinth, and cabinet positions match the before photo, while new traditional-style handles replace the straight metal pulls.
...
Against the pale cabinetry, individual colors in the brick are easier to distinguish, from deep red and brown bricks to lighter mortar joints. The glass panel behind the cooktop remains, preserving the exposed masonry around it.
...
Neptune Lily continues across the long cabinet run and up the tall units surrounding the ovens. Large cabinet doors that once displayed prominent oak grain now read through their recessed panels, proportions, and hardware instead.
...
The pale finish also changes the relationship between the cabinets and ceiling. Dark timber beams remain overhead, but they no longer repeat the brown tones of the cabinetry below, creating a clearer distinction between the old structural wood and painted kitchen units.
...
From this angle, the island provides one of the clearest comparisons with the original kitchen. Wine storage still occupies both sides of the center opening, the decorative cutout remains beneath the granite, and vertical grooves still wrap the end panel.
...
Neptune Lily connects those separate details through one pale finish while the granite top and oak floor provide darker and warmer surfaces around it. What first appears to be a different island is the same structure seen in the before photos.
...
The side-by-side view makes the extent of the change easier to see because the layout barely moves between the two images. Tall cabinetry still surrounds the ovens, the sink remains beneath the window, and the same dark granite runs across the base cabinets, yet replacing the warm oak finish with Neptune Lily changes which parts of the kitchen command attention.
...
Oak once connected the cabinets with the wood floor and ceiling beams, filling much of the view with similar brown tones. After the repaint, the floor and old beams remain as the main wood elements, while the pale cabinetry creates a stronger contrast with the granite, black ovens, and green walls.

title: Copper's Latest High-End Induction Stove Brings The Heat Better Than Ever
highlights:
Copper's Latest High-End Induction Stove Brings The Heat Better Than Ever

...
The new Charlie range now supports both 120 and 240-volt outlets, so it’s easier to install too.

 By Sam Rutherford Sept. 24, 2026 12:53 pm EST
...
Even though most people might not think of stoves as tech, the Charlie induction range was one of the most drool-worthy gadgets of CES 2025. However, today it got some upgrades that make it even more powerful and easier to install in your home.
...
Simply dubbed the new Charlie, the latest update to Copper's induction stove features four main improvements. The first is an even beefier broiler that delivers up to 3,000 watts of power, up from 2,700 watts on the previous model. Furthermore, the oven preheats significantly faster, needing just three minutes and 50 seconds to hit 350 degrees Fahrenheit. That's an improvement of 15 percent compared to the original model, which was already quite speedy with a preheat time of 4:30 for the exact same temperature. Meanwhile, the new Charlie's burners are stronger too with the range now touting 3kW induction zones instead of the 2.8kW eyes on the original.
...
However, for those looking to replace their existing range with a new one, perhaps the most important update is that the latest model is now compatible with both 120 and 240-volt outlets, instead of being limited to 120-volt sockets like its predecessor. This means that regardless of what kind of plug you have hidden behind your stove, it should be dead simple to swap in the Charlie without needing to call an electrician or rewire your kitchen. Elsewhere, the range's core features remain the same, including a built-in battery to help speed up cooking, an onboard display, precise temperature control and a flat, easy-to-wipe surface for hassle-free cleanup. And while it's not listed on the Copper's website just yet, the Charlie is also slated to get some additional aesthetic options including handles and knobs finished in cherry.
...
Behind the scenes, Copper also seems poised for expansion as the company has partnered with Miele, which will now be in charge of manufacturing Charlie ranges at its factory in Alabama. This should bring increased production and reliability to the line. Miele is one of the most well-respected home appliance brands, and the company traditionally shies away from lending its manufacturing capabilities to third
...
party products.
...
That said, the downside to the new Charlie is that it's gotten an $800 price bump over the original, bringing its cost to $6,799 for the stainless steel model or a whopping $7,199 for the walnut version. That's simply a ton of money for a stove, even one as nice and powerful as this one. But for discerning chefs who are ready to trade in their gas range for induction, alongside rivals like Impulse's fancy cooktop, the new Charlie seems like the ideal device to show why modern electric stoves are a superior way to cook.
...
Finally, for those in the northeast who want to check out the Charlie in person before forking over a bunch of money on a stove, Copper has teamed up with Royal Green to give customers the ability to see the range in showrooms across New York and New Jersey.

title: A Couple Added Wood Trim Around Their Staircase and Made the Walls Look Paneled

Wood railings, white spindles, and gray walls framed this staircase, but the large wall sections around the steps remained bare. Tracy Laverty of Right Up My Alley and her husband Steve changed those surfaces with narrow strips of pine, creating raised rectangular sections that look like built-in wall paneling.
...
The project was part of a larger staircase update that included white risers and dark-stained railings. Rather than removing the existing staircase or covering the walls with full panels, the couple worked with the structure already in place and used trim to give the entry more architectural detail.
...
Warm wood covered the handrails, newel posts, stair treads, and risers before the makeover. White spindles provided contrast, while uninterrupted gray walls filled the tall sections surrounding the stairs.
...
The handrails
...
sanded enough to rough up the surface, then the white spindles were protected with painter’s tape. Classic Black Minwax PolyShades supplied the new finish, combining stain and
...
in one product.
...
The wall treatment began with 1-by-6 pine boards ripped lengthwise to produce trim about 2.5 inches wide. Before attaching anything, the couple marked possible layouts on the walls and adjusted the spacing until the sections worked across different parts of the staircase.
...
Straight sections could follow the floor and landing, but boards meeting the staircase had to match its slope. Angles were calculated before the pieces were cut on a miter saw.
...
Rather than installing sheets of wood behind the trim, the pine pieces went onto the painted drywall. Liquid Nails and a trim nail gun secured each section after the layout and cuts were finished.
...
The wall itself remains visible inside each rectangle, which reduces the amount of lumber needed to create the paneled effect.
...
Vertical and horizontal boards divide the tall landing wall into large framed sections. On the right, another piece follows the stair angle and connects the treatment with the railing.
...
After installation, joints were caulked and rough edges sanded. One coat of water-based primer and two coats of white trim paint covered the new wood.
...
Paneling extends beneath the upper railing and along the walls beside the steps, so the treatment is visible from several points in the entry.
...
One of the clearest details appears beside the upper run of stairs, where vertical boards meet a long piece cut to follow the handrail angle.
...
depth from the

From the upper landing, the pattern continues beneath the railing and down the tall stairwell wall. Rectangular sections change size as the available wall area changes, but the trim width and white finish remain consistent.
...
From the entry, the finished staircase combines white risers, wood treads, black railings, white spindles, and raised wall trim. Existing gray paint remains above the panel treatment, preserving contrast between the upper and lower sections.
...
Materials for the broader staircase project, including wood, stain, paint, caulk, and adhesive, cost under $100 at the time.
...
No walls had to be rebuilt to create the paneled appearance. Narrow pine strips changed the flat surfaces around the staircase, while paint tied the added pieces into the existing trim and risers.
...
The before-and-after also shows how the dark railing redirects attention through the entry, with the white wall treatment filling areas that had been left plain.

title: Bosch 4V Cordless Tools Put Convenience Over Power
highlights:
The cordless-tool industry has spent years convincing buyers that every battery platform needs more power. The new Bosch 4V cordless tools arriving at Lowe’s make the opposite case: sometimes the smarter tool is the one small enough to stay in a kitchen drawer instead of living in the garage.
...
This is not Bosch discovering low-voltage tools for the first time. IXO and PSR Select have existed in other forms and markets for years. What changed on September 21, 2026 is the U.S. retail push around four compact products built specifically for cleaning, fastening, assembly and inflation. That makes the move especially interesting after Bosch spent 2026 emphasizing the kind of cordless platform depth normally associated with bigger professional tools.
...
The new U.S. assortment consists of the TAYDO 4V Max Cleaning Brush, PSR-SELECT 4V Max Multi-Bit Screwdriver, IXO 4V Max Screwdriver and PNEO 4V Max Air Pump.
...
Bosch’s September launch details are unusually clear about the intended customer. These are compact products for smaller jobs and everyday household tasks, not substitutes for an 18V hammer drill, framing saw or professional impact driver.
...
A full-size cordless drill can tighten a cabinet hinge. An 18V inflator can top up a bicycle tire. Neither automatically makes those jobs better
...
Higher voltage usually brings greater potential
...
, but it can also bring larger batteries, more weight and more
...
. More power creates overhead
...
Bosch is betting that some consumers would rather grab a purpose-built tool immediately than retrieve a more capable machine, install the correct accessory and carry extra battery mass for a two-minute repair.
...
Instead of competing primarily on torque, it stores 12 commonly used screwdriver bits inside a revolving drum. Bosch’s EasySELECT system lets the user rotate through the bits while an illuminated magnifying window shows the selected option.
...
routine household fastening
...
Anyone who owns several drills has probably spent time looking for the correct Phillips, Torx or slotted bit. PSR-SELECT tries to eliminate that interruption rather than overpower the screw.
...
Convenience becomes
...
That is a useful shift because household tool frustration often comes from setup. A machine that is technically weaker can still finish a small task faster if everything required to begin is already attached to it.
...
| Tool Class | Best Fit | Main Advantage | Main Compromise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4V compact tools | Assembly, repairs, cleaning, inflation | Low weight and quick access | Limited heavy-load capability |
| 12V tools | Installation, maintenance, lighter trade work | Compact with greater output | Larger than pocket-scale tools |
| 18V tools | Construction and demanding applications | High power and broad platform depth | More tool and battery than some tasks require |
| Corded tools | Long-duration stationary work | Continuous power | Cord management and outlet dependence |
...
Bosch rates the new U.S. IXO at up to 57 in-lbs of hard torque and claims up to 200 screws per charge under its test method. A 360-degree LED light ring surrounds the working area.
...
But assembling a bookcase does not demand impact-driver territory. Excessive speed or torque can become a disadvantage around small hardware, plastic components and inexpensive furniture fasteners.
...
PNEO is a compact air pump rated to 150 PSI, with automatic shutoff at the selected pressure, a display showing actual and target pressure, memory for three preferred pressure settings, a rotating hose and onboard adapter storage.
...
The broader PNEO technical specifications also show how deliberately compact this category is: Bosch’s international version is rated for tires, balls and other smaller inflation jobs rather than high-volume pneumatic work.
...
The cleaning brush carries an IPX5 water-resistance rating and accepts attachments intended for surfaces ranging from grout and stovetops to shower glass, footwear, vehicle wheels and outdoor furniture.
...
Bosch is not merely shrinking drills. It is applying cordless-tool design principles—motors, batteries, accessories and ergonomic housings—to household tasks that were traditionally handled manually or by unrelated appliance brands.
...
Bosch says the four-tool assortment is available through Lowe’s stores in a limited release while supplies last.
...
A broad retail launch gives Bosch something engineering tests cannot provide: evidence about which compact-tool ideas actually attract U.S. buyers.
...
Will shoppers understand why PSR-SELECT costs more complexity than a manual multi-bit screwdriver? Does a powered cleaning brush belong beside drills and drivers? Will consumers buy a dedicated 4V inflator when larger battery-platform inflators already exist?
...
A professional cordless ecosystem can succeed with buyers who deliberately research tools before purchasing. A compact household product benefits much more from immediate understanding. Someone walking a Lowe’s aisle should be able to look at PNEO or PSR-SELECT and understand the problem it removes within seconds.
...
The next development worth following is not another torque specification. It is whether Bosch turns these products into a coherent U.S. family with clear battery, charging, accessory and retail logic.
...
Bosch has already taken that approach internationally with its Daily Helper concept, grouping compact products around routine household work. The U.S. launch now tests whether the same philosophy translates into a market crowded with inexpensive cordless screwdrivers and larger battery platforms.
...
The danger is fragmentation. Four clever products are less compelling if each feels like another charger, another battery decision or another isolated gadget.
...
The opportunity is the opposite: build a small-tool system where people choose 4V precisely because they do not want the size and complexity of a professional platform.
...
That is why the Bosch 4V cordless tools matter beyond four new products at Lowe’s. They test whether the cordless market has matured enough to stop assuming that every upgrade must mean more power.
...
For demanding work, voltage and output will continue to matter. But around the house, the best tool may be the smallest one people actually reach for.

Dark cherry cabinets, ornate brass hardware, speckled granite, white appliances, and a fluorescent ceiling light gave this 30-year-old kitchen a look its new owner wanted to change. Painting the cabinets could have delivered the fastest visual shift, but the wood was one part of the room she wanted to preserve.

Reddit user Korgity bought the New England fixer-upper and chose to keep the cherry cabinetry, granite countertops, and existing footprint while directing the renovation toward the elements around them. The house needed repairs, the appliances no longer worked, fixtures had corroded, and an overgrown shrub blocked light from the kitchen window.
...
New stainless appliances, a taller window, white tile backsplash, workstation sink, new faucet, and updated lighting changed the kitchen without covering the cherry grain. Even the original brass cabinet hardware stayed, leaving much of the kitchen’s character intact while removing features that had made the room feel stuck in another decade.
...
Cherry cabinetry wrapped around the narrow kitchen, with arched upper doors, raised-panel base cabinets, crown molding, and brass hardware creating a strong traditional character. White appliances interrupted the dark cabinet runs, while a large fluorescent fixture occupied the ceiling above the workspace.
...
not in need of replacement, and their construction

the New England house, so the homeowner chose to work with them. That decision also avoided replacing a substantial amount of matching cabinetry found beyond the main cooking area.
...
Cherry was not limited to the main kitchen. A separate bar area had matching cabinets, granite counters, a small sink, and glass-front storage, extending the same millwork into another part of the home.
...
Rather than treating this area as decorative overflow, the homeowner incorporated it into the way the kitchen functions. It became a coffee station, with the sink available for cleanup and the surrounding cabinetry providing storage outside the compact main workspace.
...
Beside the kitchen, the dining room had pale yellow walls, dark wood trim, white wainscoting, and a pineapple chandelier. Large windows brought light into the room, but the wall treatment did little to connect the dining space with the traditional character of the cherry kitchen.
...
The chandelier also looked like a candidate for replacement, yet it eventually became another original feature that survived the refresh. Instead of removing it, the homeowner changed its surroundings.
...
The finished kitchen keeps the cherry cabinet doors, granite, brass hardware, and narrow footprint seen in the before photo, but the white appliances are gone. A GE Profile refrigerator, Café induction double-oven range, Miele dishwasher, and Zephyr vent bring stainless steel and darker finishes into the existing cabinet runs.
...
The fluorescent ceiling fixture was also removed, eliminating the broad white panel that once sat above the kitchen. These changes leave the cherry as an intentional wood finish rather than one dated element competing with several others.
...
A taller window with a transom now fills much more of the wall above the sink, bringing daylight into a kitchen dominated by dark cabinetry. The change became even more important after the removal of the large shrub that had blocked the original window from outside.
...
Below it, a Franke composite workstation sink and Newport Brass faucet replace the older fixtures. The drop-in sink also covers some corrosion, soap stains, and old bolt holes in the retained granite, allowing the existing counter to remain rather than forcing another replacement.
...
The backsplash changed to Adex Neri tile in a satin finish, using 3-by-12-inch white tiles with white grout. With arched cabinet doors, visible granite pattern, and ornate hardware already bringing detail to the room, the homeowner chose a quieter surface rather than another focal point.
...
She had considered replacing the granite as well, then changed her mind after seeing its lighter color, mineral variation, and depth once it was cleaned and sealed. Keeping it meant the refresh did not depend on replacing every surface associated with the original kitchen.
...
Ornate brass knobs and backplates remain across the cabinet doors and drawers, another detail that could have disappeared during a conventional update. Removing them presented its own problem because the backplates were attached with escutcheon pins that could damage the wood.
...
Cherry also darkens as it ages, so taking the backplates away could have exposed lighter marks beneath them. The homeowner left the solid brass hardware in place, allowing the aged finish and decorative cabinet fronts to remain part of the kitchen.
...
A second stretch of cherry cabinetry forms the butler’s pantry, where glass-front upper cabinets, granite counters, and base storage match the main kitchen. This area now serves as a baking station, microwave location, and extra work surface rather than sitting apart from food preparation.
...
Together with the coffee bar and an eight-foot china cabinet outside the kitchen, these spaces provide much of the storage that the narrow main room cannot accommodate.
...
The former yellow dining room now has Bobbi Beck’s Agnew scenic mural above the white wainscoting. Trees, water, architecture, and landscape scenes cover the upper walls, pushing the room toward the historical character the homeowner wanted rather than stripping away its traditional details.
...
Even the pineapple chandelier remained. The homeowner had considered it too fussy at first, but after adding the mural and working with the existing wainscoting, she decided the fixture belonged in the finished room.
...
Side by side, the kitchen makes an unusual case for leaving dark wood cabinetry alone. The cherry doors, arched profiles, granite, brass hardware, and basic footprint remain recognizable, while stainless appliances, a larger window, new backsplash, sink, faucet, and lighting change what surrounds them.
...
Instead of making the cabinets disappear beneath paint, the refresh treats them as part of the house worth keeping. The result raises a different question for anyone looking at an older wood kitchen: Are the cabinets making it feel dated, or is it everything around them?

# This couple transformed their dark, dated 1970s Bristol home into a bright California-inspired retreat
...
Playful prints, joyful colour and earthy textures bring a sunny West Coast feel to this reworked 1970s home
...
On a chilly grey day, stepping through the front door of Jacqueline Lopez’s home is a revelation. Cool and restrained on the outside, this angular slate-faced property has been completely transformed inside with playful prints, joyful colour and earthy textures to bring a sunny vibe that’s more West Coast, USA, than West Country, UK.
...
A cleverly planned house, it maximises every inch of space with a thoughtful layout and some smart storage solutions. Jacqueline has overseen almost every detail of its transformation, together with the help of an all-female team of builders, decorators and a kitchen designer. ‘I have a job in finance, but I love interiors and pore over design books. It’s definitely my creative outlet,’ she says.
...

The ground floor was completely reorganised to create a large open-plan living area. Poodle & Blonde’s Wave wallpaper was the starting point for the decor
...
Although the purchase wasn’t entirely straightforward – it was a probate sale – and the interiors badly needed updating, the couple were able to see beyond the existing decor. ‘We lived here for six weeks to get a feel for the light and layout before deciding what needed to change. Then we moved out and rented locally for five months while the building work was under way because every corner of the house needed attention.’
...
In order to reorientate the living spaces so they would look out onto the south-west-facing garden, the ground floor was completely reorganised. ‘There was a huge brick chimney breast running through the centre of the house. It made everything feel dark and divided, and continued up into a fireplace on the first floor. Removing it to create a large open-plan living area meant installing a structural steel beam,’ Jacqueline explains. ‘The original kitchen, tucked away at the front of the house behind a small serving hatch, also felt disconnected from the rest of the space.’

To help reimagine the layout, the couple enlisted designer Francesca Gaskin of Jetsam Made in Bristol, who created bespoke cabinetry for the kitchen, utility room and upstairs bathroom. ‘We initially considered shiny floors,’ Jacqueline says, ‘but instead chose rustic herringbone tiles in a soft matt finish. I like the contrast with the more polished, glamorous furnishings.’ Upstairs, herringbone oak parquet echoes the same pattern, grounding the interiors with warmth and texture.

title: Why You Should Add a 95% Day to Your DIY Routine

Why You Should Add a 95% Day to Your DIY Routine

# Why I’m Adding a “95% Day” to Every DIY Project From Now On

 

 koldunova/Getty Images 

By Alex Shoemaker 

Family Handyman's Editorial Process

Published on Sep. 23, 2026
...
Make today the day you finally tackle those nagging chores on your DIY home improvement list and finish old projects.
...
Well, enough is enough. I’m finally making a plan to tackle these annoying final steps. Learn what a 95% day is, why, if you’re a DIYer like me, you should consider doing it as well, and other tips to stop putting off those end-of-project steps.
...
## What Is a 95% Day?
...
Simply put, a 95% day should be used exclusively to go around and finish the things in your house you’ve been putting off. That doesn’t mean starting a new renovation, or even making more progress on one you recently started or are still far from finishing. Instead, it means tackling those small, annoying things on projects that were never “fully” completed. You know, things that are 95% done.
...
One of the best examples, and the one I’m most guilty of, is installing trim. I’m currently sitting in my living room, writing this essay about self-discipline while 25 feet away I can see a small gap where, months later, I still haven’t added trim for my “finished” kitchen remodel.
...
Replacing outlet covers, painting new drywall, filling nail holes, and installing cabinet hardware are other small fixes that would have taken a project from 95% done to actually done done, but for some reason took months to do.
...
As I’m writing this, I’m realizing part of that reasoning is that doing a new renovation rather than tackling those last little steps feels like a better ROI on my time. Getting the bathroom gutted while the kitchen looks finished to the untrained eye gets me closer to having this house in
...
state I want it to be in.
...
## Why You Should Add a 95% Day to Your DIY Routine
...
I’d be lying if I said this is the first time I’ve done a 95% day. The last was when my wife and I were in the process of listing our home for sale, and we finally did all those annoying little things that the next homeowners would get to enjoy longer than we ever did.
...
A quarterly 95% day has officially been added to the calendar. By putting the event into written, or typed, form, I now have a digital reminder to hold myself accountable.
...
That trim in the kitchen is getting added. The light bulb in the bathroom vanity that burned out is getting replaced. The drawer slide that sticks and needs to be yanked open with the force of 1,000 Hulks? Yep, that’s on the list too.
...
So if you’re a typical DIYer who feels personally attacked by this essay, know you’re not alone. Consider adding a 95% day to your DIY routine, and finally give yourself the satisfaction of calling those almost-finished projects actually finished.

title: "Boob Lights" Are Making Your Home Look Tacky. Here's How Designers Fix Them
highlights:
"Boob Lights" Are Making Your Home Look Tacky. Here's How Designers Fix Them
...
The typical rental apartment “ landlord special” tends to come with a familiar set of design details: doorknobs layered with paint, uneven wall patches, and the infamous flush-mount ceiling fixture better known as the “boob light.” Anyone who has spent time in a rental has probably seen one—they’re often installed in nearly every room. From my college apartment in Iowa to my current Manhattan apartment, these fixtures have been a recurring part of my living spaces. After years of looking up at those glass domes, I finally decided it was time to do something about them.
...
From a design standpoint, these lights leave a lot to be desired. Their shape feels clunky and cartoonish, yet they rarely provide the kind of illumination a room actually needs. Many boast frosted glass shades meant to soften bright light, but instead, they often make spaces feel dim and dull.
...
When the glass isn’t frosted, the opposite problem happens, and the light can feel overly harsh. And renters aren’t the only ones dealing with them. A quick scroll through Zillow listings shows that many new-build homes still include these fixtures. Despite their widespread revulsion, landlords and house flippers continue installing them largely because they’ve traditionally been cheap to manufacture.
...
If you’re trying to disguise your boob lights—or at least make them a little easier on the eyes—we asked designers to share their favorite ideas for concealing or replacing these all-too-common fixtures.
...
As the saying goes, if it ain't broke, don't fix it. The boob light was created for the same reasons it’s still so commonly found today. “I think it's just the cheapest possible solution for a landlord to stick a light on the ceiling. I'd be surprised if one in your apartment costs $19,” says David Calligeros, founder of Remains Lighting Company. “There are a few really good ones, and there are a lot of ubiquitous, ugly ones.”
...
Although it's annoying that boob lights persist despite widespread disapproval, we're lucky to live in a time when replacing these less-than-titillating light fixtures is relatively easy and can be done without touching the wiring at all.
...
## How Can I Replace My Boob Light?
...
Before swapping out your boob light for a more attractive fixture, there are a few things to keep in mind, with ceiling height being the most important one.
...
“If you've got ample ceiling height, then you don't want a flush mount. You want a hanging pendant or chandelier or something that drops into the space deeper and is more expansive,” Calligeros says. However, for a shorter ceiling, Saft suggests “a drum shade or something on a smaller scale that is not coming down from the ceiling.”
...
The room's purpose matters, too. Even if you have tall ceilings in your bedroom, you likely wouldn't want to install a huge, metal pendant light. “For the bedroom, I'll move away from glass shades. I usually like to look for something that has fabric and has a softness and warmth to it, and obviously going a little bit closer to the ceiling depending upon the walk space and flow of the room,” Saft explains. In a dining room or entryway, he suggests using a more dramatic fixture with multiple arms.
...
Both Saft and Calligeros, however, believe the bedroom should always have light coming from different directions and would suggest floor lamps and table lamps to complete your lighting formula.
...
For renters or anyone who doesn't want to make a drastic rewiring change to their overhead lighting, there's good news. Tulip Shades is a brand that offers aesthetically pleasing shades that fit right on top of your existing boob lights. The ceiling mount attaches with tape, and the shade connects with magnets, making switching out your shades a quick and easy task.
...
“Lighting is, in my opinion, the most important thing you can change in a space to really make a difference,” says Lori Smyth, the founder of Tulip Shades. “We don't want to be haters of the boob lights: There are times, and there are places that they are completely appropriate and they work. But there are other areas, for example, in a bedroom or a living room, where the lighting is just too harsh. It doesn't really help your mood; it doesn't help you feel better.”
...
If you plan to be in your space for a few years, replacing the boob lights in your rental is a worthwhile upgrade. Using a Tulip Shade is completely renter-friendly, but completely replacing your boob light is one of the least obtrusive changes you can make in your home.
...
“Without reference to whatever God-awful wiring might be in one's ceiling, a light fixture is pretty easy to change,” Calligeros says. “They're usually mounted with either two screws directly to the junction box, and three minutes after you're up on the ladder, the fixture is down and in the recycling. Then the sky's the limit.”

title: What's happening to UK interest rates and mortgage deals? - BBC
highlights:
The Bank of England has held UK interest rates at 3.75% for a fifth time, keeping them at the lowest level since February 2023.
...
Before the US-Israeli war with Iran, rates had been expected to fall in 2026, but the economic fallout from the conflict has pushed up inflation across the globe, making cuts unlikely.
...
Interest rates affect mortgage, credit card and savings rates for millions of people.
...
An interest rate tells you how much it costs to borrow money, or the reward for saving it.
...
The Bank of England's base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what they charge their own customers for mortgages as well as the interest rate they pay on savings.
...
The Bank moves its base rate up and down in order to keep UK inflation — the rate at which prices are increasing — at or near 2%.
...
When inflation is above that target, the Bank typically puts rates up. 

The idea is to encourage people to spend less, reducing demand for goods and services and limiting price rises.
...
The Bank of England's base rate rose to 5.25% in 2023. It remained at that level until August 2024, when the Bank started cutting.
...
Five cuts brought rates down to 4%, before the Bank held rates at its meetings in September and November 2025. 

It then cut in December 2025 before holding rates steady in January, March, April, June and July 2026.
...
Meanwhile, the main UK inflation measure, CPI, has dropped significantly since the high of 11.1% recorded in October 2022 as a result of the war in Ukraine.

It was 2.9% in the year to July 2026, up from 2.6% the previous month.
...
The Office for National Statistics (ONS), which tracks UK inflation, said the uptick was a result of higher energy costs.
...
The US-Israel war with Iran has put up energy and fuel costs around the world which has increased the pace of price rises more generally.
...
At the start of the year, the Bank had been expected to cut interest rates twice in 2026, with the first drop predicted to come in March or April.
...
However, the increase in fuel prices and inflation after the outbreak of the conflict has upended all of this. Oil prices initially rose sharply as a result of disruption to supplies in the region, but dropped back when various ceasefires were agreed.
...
Oil prices rose again when the US and Iran resumed attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in July.
...
"Inflation has fallen faster than we'd expected, but the conflict in the Middle East continues to mean high and volatile energy prices," said the Bank's governor, Andrew Bailey. 

"That will cause inflation to rise again later this year. However the conflict unfolds, our job is to make sure any increase in inflation is temporary and that it comes back to our 2% target."
...
UK household energy bills rose after the latest increase in the price cap which took effect on 1 July, which could push UK inflation higher.
...
Given the uncertainty, many analysts think rates are likely to stay at 3.75% for the foreseeable future. 

Getty Images
...
Just under a third of households have a mortgage, according to the government's English Housing Survey.
...
About 500,000 homeowners have a mortgage that "tracks" the Bank of England's rate. That means any cut means a reduction in the monthly repayments on their outstanding loan.
...
An additional 500,000 homeowners on standard variable (SVR) rates rely on their lender choosing to pass on any Bank rate cut.
...
But the vast majority of mortgage customers - some 87% - have fixed-rate deals. While their monthly payments aren't immediately affected by a rate change, their future deals are.
...
As at 30 July, the average rate on a new two-year fixed deal was 5.62%, up from 4.83% at the start of March, according to the financial information service Moneyfacts.
...
For those looking for a five-year deal, the average rate was 5.66%, up from 4.95% over the same period.
...
The average two-year tracker rate was 4.51%.
...
About 800,000 fixed-rate mortgages with an interest rate of 3% or below are expected to expire every year, on average, until the end of 2027. Borrowing costs for customers coming off those deals are likely to rise sharply.

Mortgage
...
Bank of England interest rates also influence the amount charged on credit cards, bank loans and car loans.
...
Lenders can decide to reduce their own interest rates if Bank cuts make borrowing costs cheaper.

However, this tends to happen very slowly.
...
The Bank base rate also affects how much savers earn on their money.
...
A falling base rate is likely to mean a reduction in the returns offered to savers by banks and building societies and vice versa. 

As at 29 July, Moneyfacts said the average rate for an easy access savings account based on a balance of £10,000 was 2.55%. The average rate for an easy access cash ISA was 2.73%.
...
The average rate for customers who were prepared to lock their money away for a year was 4.27%. 

Cuts in rates particularly affect those who rely on the interest from their savings to top up their income.
...
In June 2024, the European Central Bank (ECB) started cutting the main interest rate for the eurozone from an all-time high of 4%, falling to 2% in June 2025.
...
However, in June 2026, the ECB raised rates to 2.25% as it reacted to the Iran war.
...
The US central bank - the Federal Reserve - has cut interest rates three times since September 2025, taking them to the current range of 3.5% to 3.75%, the lowest since 2022.
...
The Fed most recently voted to hold rates at that level at its July meeting, the second under new chair Kevin Warsh.
...
US President Donald Trump had repeatedly attacked the previous Fed chair Jerome Powell for not cutting rates.
...
Warsh is expected to be generally more supportive of cuts, but will also have to respond to the fallout from the Iranian conflict.

To budget money, follow the five steps below.
...
A budgeting system is a plan for how to use your money. Everyone has different habits, personality types and approaches to managing money, and there are systems that can fit your lifestyle. 

Every budget should cover your needs, some wants and savings for emergencies and the future.
...
Examples of budgeting systems include the envelope system, the zero-based budget, and the 50/30/20 budget, in which 50% of your take-home pay goes toward necessities, 30% toward wants and 20% toward savings and retirement.
...
60/20/20 and 60/30/10, may work well for some situations.
...
Pay attention to where your money is going. If you notice areas where you’re overspending, try to cut those costs. If you’re able to make cuts and have money left over, put it toward debt repayment, savings or another financial priority.
...
### Step 4. Automate your savings
...
Set up automatic savings to make things easier. You can set automatic deposits to an emergency fund, investment or retirement account on your paydays.
...
If your income changes from month to month, set reminders to move money when you can. You don't have to do it alone — a friend or online group can keep you motivated to stick to your budget.
...
Your money situation will change over time. Check your budget every few months and adjust if needed. 

If you find that the initial budgeting system you chose isn’t working for you, consider trying a different strategy. The budget you choose doesn’t have to last forever.
...
## Determine your budgeting priorities 

When budgeting, it can be hard to figure out which items are most urgent. Should you prioritize your credit card debt, student loan repayments or retirement savings? Here is a list of potential priorities from most to least urgent. 

Priority No. 1: Start an emergency fund. Priority No. 1:
...
Many experts recommend trying to build up several months of bare-bones living expenses. NerdWallet suggests starting an emergency fund of at least $500, which could be enough to cover small emergencies and repairs. If that starting amount isn’t possible, put at least a little bit toward the fund every paycheck.
...
Priority No. 3: Pay off high-interest debt. Priority No. 3: Pay off high-interest debt.
...
A NerdWallet study found that 30% of Americans plan on paying off one or more of their debts in full in 2026
...
If this is one of your goals, focus on high-interest credit card debt or loans, such as personal and payday loans, title loans and rent-to-own payments.

 Look into ways to help with your debt — like a debt management plan or bankruptcy — if either of these things is true for you:
...
- You can't repay your credit cards, medical bills or personal loans (i.e., unsecured debt) in the next five years, even if you cut your spending a lot.

- Your total debt (not including things like a mortgage or car loan) is as much or more than half of what you make before taxes.
...
Priority No. 4: Save for retirement (again). Priority No. 4: Save for retirement (again).
...
Once you've paid off your high-interest debt and have some extra money, focus on saving for retirement. Financial experts suggest saving 10-15% of your income before taxes for retirement. For many people, that's a goal to work towards over time. Just know that your company match, if offered, counts toward that 15% total. 

If your job doesn't offer a 401(k), or if you’ve already put in enough to get the full match, you can look into other options, such as a Roth or traditional IRA.
...
Keep adding to your emergency savings. Try to build up enough to cover three to six months of basic living expenses — like rent, groceries and utilities. 

It might take a long time to reach this goal. That's OK. Use the fund when emergencies happen, and try to put the money back when you can.
...
Priority No. 6: Pay down the rest of your debt. Priority No. 6: Pay down the rest of your debt. 

Once your emergency fund is in good shape and your retirement savings are on track, focus on other debts. These payments go beyond the minimum required to pay off debt, if you have any remaining.
...
If you’ve already paid off your high-interest debt, what’s left is probably lower-rate, such as student loans, or tax-deductible debt like your mortgage. Tackle these when the goals listed above are covered.
...
Priority No. 7: Save for yourself. Priority No. 7: Save for yourself. 

Great job! If you've taken all the steps above, you're in a great position. You’ve built smart money habits and now have more freedom with your money. 

To earn more on your savings, think about using a high-yield savings account. These often pay more than regular savings accounts. 

You can divide your savings into different buckets — one for emergencies, one for car repairs and one for fun. Some banks will automatically move your monthly interest earnings to your bucket of choice, helping you reach your goals faster. The more you save, the more your money grows. It's a win-win.
...
## Try a simple budgeting plan: 50/30/20
...
One popular budget plan is the 50/30/20 budget. If you stick to this plan, you can handle your bills, save for the future, prepare for emergencies and enjoy life, too. 

### Allow up to 50% of your income for needs
...
Your necessities — about 50% of your after-tax income — should include:

- Groceries.
- Housing.
- Basic utilities.
- Transportation.
- Insurance.
- Minimum loan and credit card payments. Anything beyond the minimum goes into the savings and debt repayment category.
- Child care or other expenses you need so you can work.
...
If your basic needs go over 50%, you can use some of your “wants” money for now. That's OK. But if those needs are going over 50% month after month, consider switching to another budgeting model. Switching your budget isn't a sign of failure. Budgets should work for your life.

If your necessities fall under the 50% cap, review the expenses that stay the same every month, often called fixed expenses. title: 5 Ways to Budget During Inflation | Gerald Cash Advance & Buy Now Pay Later
highlights:
- Track expenses ruthlessly to identify where inflation hits hardest and where you can trim spending without sacrificing essentials
- Prioritize debt payoff before inflation erodes the value of your future dollars—focus on variable-rate debt first
- Build a flexible emergency fund to handle unexpected costs and avoid high-interest borrowing when inflation spikes
- Shift spending toward assets that hold value during inflation rather than cash that loses purchasing power
- Create an income-first budget that allocates money as soon as it arrives, rather than spending first and budgeting leftovers
...
The good news: you don't need to earn more to weather inflation. You need to spend smarter. This guide covers five practical ways to budget during inflation, plus specific tactics you can implement today. If you're looking for how to borrow $50 instantly for an unexpected expense or want to restructure your entire budget, these strategies will help you keep more money in your pocket when inflation pressures your finances.
...
| Strategy | What It Does | Time to Implement | Difficulty Level |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Track Every Expense | Reveals where inflation hits hardest and identifies waste | 3-4 hours | Easy |
| Pay Down Variable-Rate Debt | Reduces interest burden as rates rise with inflation | Ongoing | Medium |
| Build Emergency Fund | Prevents expensive borrowing when surprises hit | 3-6 months | Medium |
| Shift Discretionary Spending | Protects purchasing power by avoiding cash erosion | 1-2 weeks | Medium |
| Income-First Budget | Allocates money before spending to prevent lifestyle creep | 1 week to set up | Hard |
...
Here's a counterintuitive truth: inflation erodes the real value of debt. If you owe $10,000 today and inflation runs at 5% annually, that debt is worth about $9,750 in real terms a year from now. But there's a catch—only if your interest rate is fixed.
...
-rate debt like credit cards, adjustable-rate mortgages, and some personal loans gets worse as inflation rises. Banks raise rates to keep pace. Your monthly payment balloons. This
...
Prioritize paying down balances and other variable debt first. Even an extra $50 monthly toward a plastic card carrying 18% APR saves you hundreds in interest. Once variable debt is gone, your budget has breathing room. Fixed-rate debt (like a mortgage at 3.5%) actually becomes easier to manage during inflation because your payment stays the same while your earnings ideally grow.
...
Start small. $500 is better than $0. $1,000 is even better. The goal is to cover one or two months of essential expenses (housing, food, utilities, insurance). During inflation, this buffer keeps you from derailing your budget when unexpected costs hit. You can learn how to handle household income during inflation with practical emergency strategies that protect your family.
...
Cash loses purchasing power during inflation. $1,000 sitting in a savings account earning 0.01% interest is worth about $950 in real terms after a year of 5% inflation. That's not a strategy—that's losing money slowly.
...
This doesn't mean you need to become an investor. It means being intentional about where discretionary dollars go. Instead of letting extra money sit in a checking account, consider modest alternatives: a high-yield savings account earning 4-5%, Treasury I-Bonds, or even strategic spending on durable goods before prices rise further.
...
If you know your heating costs will jump 10% next winter, buying an efficient space heater now (before the price increase) is smarter than waiting. If you use a particular household product regularly, stocking up before inflation hits again makes sense. The key is distinguishing between panic-buying (which creates clutter) and strategic purchasing (which protects your budget).
...
Most budgets fail because they're reactive. You spend, then try to budget what's left. During inflation, there's never anything left. An income-first budget flips the script: money gets allocated the moment it arrives.
...
Here's how it works. The moment your paycheck hits your bank account, money gets divided into categories before you spend a dime. Fifty percent goes to essentials (housing, utilities, food, insurance). Thirty percent goes to debt payoff and savings. Twenty percent is discretionary. These percentages are flexible—adjust based on your situation—but the principle is fixed: plan first, spend second.
...
This approach works during inflation because it forces prioritization. You can't accidentally overspend on dining out if that money is already earmarked for groceries. You can't raid your savings for a vacation if it's in a separate account. The structure protects you from inflation's psychological pressure to "just spend it"—because every dollar has a job before you touch it.
...
Inflation is a pressure test for your budget. It exposes gaps, forces hard choices, and demands discipline. But it's not unbeatable. Track your spending ruthlessly. Cut debt strategically. Build an emergency fund. Protect your purchasing power. And structure your budget so money has a purpose before you spend it.
...
The households that weather inflation best aren't those with the highest incomes—they're the ones with intentional spending plans and systems that survive shocks. Start with one strategy this week. Track your expenses. Identify one variable-rate debt to attack. Build a $500 emergency fund. The momentum builds from there.
...
The 70-10-10-10 rule is a simplified budget framework that allocates your after-tax income as follows: 70% for essential expenses (housing, food, utilities, insurance), 10% for debt repayment, 10% for savings and emergency funds, and 10% for discretionary spending. This structure is popular because it's easy to remember and works well during inflation—it forces you to prioritize essentials before lifestyle spending. Your actual percentages may differ based on your situation, but the principle remains: divide income intentionally before you spend it.
...
During high inflation, diversification protects your purchasing power. Keep essentials in a high-yield savings account (earning 4-5% interest currently). Consider Treasury I-Bonds, which adjust rates based on inflation and offer protection against purchasing power loss. Pay down variable-rate debt aggressively—this provides a guaranteed 'return' equal to your interest rate. For longer-term money, inflation-protected investments like Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) or dividend-paying stocks can help. Avoid holding large cash balances in low-interest accounts, as inflation erodes their value faster than interest can compensate.
...
During hyperinflation (extreme cases like 10%+ annually), wealth preservation shifts dramatically. Avoid holding cash—it becomes worthless fast. Prioritize paying down all debt, especially fixed-amount debt like mortgages (because you'll repay in cheaper dollars). Shift toward tangible assets: real estate, commodities, or durable goods with real value. International currencies or assets may provide stability. In severe hyperinflation, many people shift spending toward consumables and necessities they'll use anyway, rather than letting money sit idle. For most readers in the US, moderate inflation (3-5%) is the concern—the strategies in this article address that level effectively.
...
The five core strategies are: track spending to identify waste, pay down variable-rate debt first, build an emergency fund to avoid costly borrowing, shift discretionary spending toward value-holding assets, and use an income-first budget to allocate money before you spend it. Additionally, negotiate bills (insurance, phone, internet), cut subscriptions ruthlessly, and look for ways to increase income (side work, asking for a raise). The combination of expense reduction and income growth is most powerful, but if income growth isn't possible, the five strategies above will maximize what you have.

title: Speech by Governor Barr on housing - Federal Reserve Board
highlights:

Moreover, risks to achieving our inflation target have increased, while risks to the labor market have receded. We needed to recalibrate monetary policy to reflect the balance of risks to our mandate goals. The FOMC took important action to that end last week by increasing the policy rate, which I supported. In my view, given changes to the economy, we were out of position, and we made an adjustment in the right direction. In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion. We want to support sustainable, durable growth in support of maximum employment, and price stability is crucial to that.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta maintains a Home Ownership Affordability Monitor (Monitor) that includes an affordability index, in which a value below 100 indicates a median-income family would not be able to afford a median-priced home given the current mortgage rate. According to the Monitor, homes were, on average, affordable after the housing price crash of 2006 until the COVID-19 pandemic hit, when the affordability index fell sustainably below the threshold of 100 and kept falling to a value of 68 in July 2026, the lowest in 21 years. 2 Real, constant-quality house prices are at a record high in many places around the country. 3 Another obvious factor that affects the cost of buying a home is mortgage rates. Mortgage rates are high relative to the pre-pandemic level. This combination of high prices and high rates puts homeownership out of reach for many families. Some ask what the role of the Fed is when it comes to mortgage rates. Our short-term policy rates affect longer-term borrowing rates, including those for mortgages, but many other things affect mortgage rates as well. As I noted earlier, the Fed pursues its mandate to foster maximum employment and stable prices. Mortgage rates are generally lower when inflation is lower, and we are working toward that goal.
...
With respect to the rental market, affordability is also a problem for many households. In 1980, 55 percent of rental housing units rented for $1,000 or less. 4 Adjusting for inflation, that $1,000 would be about $3,500 today, but only 20 percent of homes rent for less than that price. 5 Today, about one-half of all renters are cost burdened, meaning they pay 30 percent or more of their income on rent, and about one-fourth of renters dedicate at least half of their income to rent. 6 It's true that, on a quality-adjusted basis, the rent increases track improvements in housing quality and amenities, but that is little comfort for someone who cannot afford the high rent burden that follows. Families need affordable shelter.
...
One side of the affordability challenge is income and savings and to what extent wages and salaries keep pace with housing costs. Over the past two decades, inflation-adjusted household incomes have risen far more slowly than home prices: Between 2000 and 2024, real median household income increased roughly 17 percent, while real U.S. house prices increased approximately 70 percent. 7 Lagging incomes compound the challenge of accumulating enough cash to get through the upfront costs of both buying and renting. According to the Federal Reserve's Report on the Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households, 68 percent of prospective first-time buyers in 2024 said they could not afford a down payment. 8 Renters face a similar cash flow barrier when moving into a new place: Upfront costs can include the first month's rent, security deposit, application fees, and sometimes the last month's rent. Fannie Mae found that affording the upfront costs of renting is a leading financial pain point when renting or moving into a new rental home. 9
...
Another recent factor that has made homeownership less affordable is high mortgage interest rates, as I mentioned earlier. Many families benefited from very low mortgage rates before 2022; these households are now less likely to move given the high rates they would face. This lock-in effect reduces both demand and supply and thus housing market dynamism. About half of all mortgages still carry rates of 4 percent or lower, and nearly 80 percent have a rate below 6 percent. 22 In tight housing markets, the lock-in effect can raise home prices because the reduction in housing supply associated with fewer homeowners selling can outweigh the corresponding reduction in demand. 23
...
So prospective homeowners face higher prices for homes, higher mortgage rates, higher home insurance costs, and higher property taxes.
...
Turning to shelter costs for renters. The inflationary period since the start of the pandemic has been extremely difficult. In August of this year, the consumer price index for rent of primary residence was 34 percent higher than it was in December 2019. Shelter cost inflation has eased considerably from its 2022–23 pace, but shelter prices are still rising at an annual rate of about 2¾ percent. While slower rent inflation should provide some relief over time, the higher level of rents remains a significant burden for many households, particularly lower-income renters. 24 As I noted at the outset, rent-to-income ratios have grown significantly, and while quality has improved, income-stressed households are spending much more of their hard-earned dollars on shelter costs.
...
The Role of the Community Reinvestment Act, the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, and Other Efforts The Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), enacted in 1977, has promoted housing affordability by encouraging banks to serve LMI communities, expanding homeownership access, and supporting affordable housing and community development investments. The CRA is a cornerstone of U.S. affordable housing policy, and the Fed is responsible for administering the act for banks we supervise.
...
In 2024 alone, CRA-related incentives supported over $430 billion in loans and investments for homeownership, small businesses, and affordable housing in these areas. This leverage of private capital helps expand the supply of affordable rental housing, often in partnership with local community-based organizations and the public sector. 25 The CRA has expanded homeownership opportunities for LMI families, such as through down-payment assistance and partnership with community development financial institutions (CDFIs). More recently, many banks and nonbank mortgage providers have been using alternative cash flow underwriting to expand access to credit for prospective homebuyers.
...
Similarly, the CRA bolsters the effectiveness of the low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC), which has been a fundamental resource for financing affordable housing for 40 years. When banks invest in LIHTC developments, they not only receive tax credits but also earn CRA consideration for supporting housing in underserved areas. Together, the CRA creates the expectation to invest, and the LIHTC provides the tool to do it, leveraging private capital to build safe, stable, and affordable apartments that strengthen families and communities. 26 On average, the LIHTC creates 110,000 units of affordable housing per year, about 4 million apartments since its enactment. 27 More broadly, multifamily construction is a key component of any strategy to improve access to affordable housing for low- and moderate-income families.
...
Recent legislation may also play a role in supporting housing accessibility. Congress recently passed bipartisan legislation that includes provisions for expanding rental assistance, guidelines for addressing zoning barriers to production, homeownership counseling and financial literacy, commercial conversions to housing, and support for manufactured housing. 28

title: What happens to the economy when Treasury yields soar
highlights:
- Treasury yields surged Wednesday, signaling potential broader impact on the U.S. economy, particularly for consumers.
- Rates along the curve hit highs not seen in years, with implications for longer- and shorter-term borrowing costs.
- The moves came amid heightened expectation that the Fed will approve another rate hike in October.
...
Soaring Treasury yields aren't just bad for the government and its $40 trillion debt. They also threaten to raise borrowing costs, hitting everyone from homeowners to credit-card users, while providing limited relief to consumer and potential benefits to banks.
...
Government debt costs leaped higher Wednesday, the product of multiple factors including a fresh report showing higher inflation pressures, surging expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in October, and an auction for 5-year notes showing that Treasury demand was weak. Competition from hyperscaler debt issuance also is seen as an aggravating factor.
...
Yields responded by jumping more than they have in nearly a year and a half, dating back to April 2025 when President Donald Trump first announced so-called reciprocal tariffs against U.S. trading partners. Recent market liquidity efforts pushed by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have had no impact so far, with rates surging higher despite intensified buyback efforts on longer-dated debt.
...
The 10-year note, a benchmark for mortgages and other longer-term borrowing, saw its yield hit, 5.125%, a level not seen since prior to the global financial crisis. Similarly, the 2-year note, which typically responds to Fed rate expectations and signals rates for home equity, auto loans and other debt, climbed more than 13 basis points past 4.9% as traders priced in a strong possibility that the central bank would follow its hike last week with another in October.
...
Such moves generally portend higher borrowing rates that hit the U.S. economy where it hurts the most — consumers, who drive nearly 70% of all economic activity and hold nearly $19 trillion in total debt.
...
While savers will benefit with incrementally higher rates on their bank savings accounts, it's unlikely to offset the pain they'll feel elsewhere, said Dan North, senior economist with Allianz Trade North America.
...
"The consumer's the most important part of the economy," North said. "They're going from little tiny yields on savings to ever slightly bigger tiny yields on savings. So I don't think that really yet helps the consumer that much. But it sure does crush housing, and it [impacts] on those all those personal consumer loans, the credit cards and so forth."
...
Indeed, the interest rate on plain-vanilla savings accounts is around 0.37% and has been on a modest decline since the Fed enacted three quarter-point cuts late in 2025, according to FDIC data.
...
Mortgage rates, though, have been on an entirely different trajectory and are likely to continue rising. A typical 30-year mortgage is now at 7.26%, up more than a quarter percentage point in just the past couple weeks and nearly a full point over the past year, according to Mortgage News Daily.
...
Credit card interest rates have been fairly steady over the past few years, but also are unlikely to stay that way if current trends hold up.
...
When the Fed hikes, it feeds directly into the prime rate, which is used as a baseline for adjustable-rate credit and most recently was at 7%, after rising a quarter point off last week's Fed move.
...
Taken together, the factors make it more expensive for consumers to borrow and less likely that they'll seek the loans and credit that fuel a lot of the activity in the $32 trillion U.S. economy.
...
"You raise the fed funds rate, rates in the short term and effectively all along the curve go up," North said. whatever benefit savers get, banks can benefit. Persistently higher yields, though, pose dangers to that growth picture.
...
"Smaller and medium enterprises are going to be suffering the worst because they have less ability to borrow," North said. "Less availability of credit makes it more difficult."

# New $

...
“Sushi Juggling Cats” may sound like the sort of game thing that a child might blurt out on a chaotic car ride when they’re overtired, but that’s also the point. EverBoard was announced Thursday morning as a new $499.99 digital game table launching exclusively through Best Buy this holiday season. The company is betting that families want more than just digital versions of Monopoly and Scrabble — it wants to use AI to let imaginations run wild.
...
In responses provided exclusively to Polygon, the company revealed new details about how EverVibe uses generative AI to create games, what safeguards it uses to protect younger players, and how much continued access to its defining feature will cost.
...
Using EverVibe will require more than the initial $499.99 hardware purchase. Every EverBoard includes one month of EverPass, the platform’s subscription service, which provides access to its full library and the capacity for five Game Creator creations per month. EverPass costs $29 for three months or $99 annually.
...
EverPass Premium costs an additional $50 per year and offers five times the “creation power”: up to 25 quick games per month, five enhanced games, or a combination of the two. EverBoard says those allowances remain subject to change as it continues testing and developing EverVibe.
...
Without an active subscription, owners can still access a free starter collection of 10 games. Resubscribing restores the full catalog, which EverBoard says will include more than 50 games at launch and additional releases released monthly.
...
Confirmed Hasbro games so far include Monopoly, Connect 4, Chutes and Ladders, and Scrabble, along with puzzles, drawing activities, arcade-style games, and other original experiences. Hasbro also owns Clue, Risk, Battleship, Candy Land, The Game of Life, and plenty of other classic board games, but it’s unclear which will be included.
...
EverBoard is far from the first company to pitch a large touchscreen as the future of family game night. When I reviewed Arcade1Up’s Infinity Game Table in 2021, I compared it to the Amazon Kindle: one device capable of storing a growing library of familiar board games. It supports six players and used to include digital Hasbro games — until that license expired. Half a decade later, as AI has become increasingly more prevalent, EverBoard looks and probably feels rather familiar to the Infinity Game Table with the obvious upgrades.
...
More recently, Board pursued the same intersection of physical and digital play from another direction, utilizing bespoke physical components to play games intended specifically for its 24-inch display.
...
Aside from the privacy films, EverBoard doesn’t seem to have much in terms of accessories at this point. And it seems to marry everything that the Infinity Game Table and Board have to offer: licensed Hasbro board games on a digital touchscreen alongside other bespoke gaming experiences. The key difference here is that you get to create your own games as well. It’s also smaller and more portable, because it runs on a battery and doesn’t require continuous AC power. Even without EverVibe, it would feel like the natural next step forward for this kind of console.
